tested:
W17 gaps (NPX-1814, rule #59): "cisco-iosvl2"/"iosvl2" used to be their OWN profiles
(512 MB, no QEMU pin, virtio-net-pci) - a second, undocumented set of hardware defaults for
the SAME Cisco IOSvL2 product EVE-NG ships as viosl2.yml (1024 MB, QEMU 2.4.0, e1000). A
folder named "iosvl2-<ver>" imported through the API therefore booted on system QEMU with half
the RAM of the identical file imported through the drop-folder (named vios_l2-*, viosl2
profile). Live-proven on VM 708 (2026-09-26): same iosvl2-2020 qcow2, API import -> 512 MB /
QEMU 10.2, drop-folder import -> 1024 MB / QEMU 2.4.0. They are now plain aliases of "viosl2"
(see the PROFILES["iosvl2"] alias block below) so the two names can never disagree again.

reasons.day0_channel: NPX-4299 (rule #59, the project owner 30 Oct 2026): FAT config DISK as hdb holding ios_config.txt (GNS3 way, CVAC); EVE-NG has no boot-time vIOS config - see providers/day0_iso_channels.py FatConfigDiskChannel.
reasons.emulator:
cpu_model host + qemu_arch x86_64 (2026-08-20, netplex rule #33 - EVE-NG's real
viosl2.yml: `qemu_arch: x86_64`, `-cpu host`; previously qemu64/i686 here, the
LLA-008 divergence). Live serial.log on netplex's own viosl2-15.2.4.55e with the old
values: a memory-pool corruption dump -> %Software-forced reload, then on reboot
"CPU exception occurred: Overflow(4) ... Unexpected exception to CPU: vector 4,
PC/EIP = 0x8E1659" - deterministic, CPU-level, reproduced with virtio extras OFF.
reasons.qemu_version_default: NPX-1810 rule #59: EVE viosl2.yml pin; 2.4.0 is built since NPX-1139 (same revert as vios, NPX-1266); needs live re-verify
reasons.min_ram_mb:
min/default_ram_mb 512/1024, not 512/768 (2026-09-12, Wave 21 close, netplex rule
#33 - rechecked EVE-NG's own viosl2.yml: `ram: 1024`, not 768). Live-reproduced on
netplex's own viosl2-15.2.4.55e with the OLD 768 value: the exact same
"Corrupted redzone blk ... alloc ... InUse" heap-corruption panic this profile's own
comment already documents, immediately followed by the "CPU exception ... vector 4"
crash - both symptoms are consistent with IOS's internal memory pools running out of
room at 768MB (a redzone/guard-byte corruption report IS a heap allocator complaining
about running out of headroom, not a CPU/virtio config issue, which the 2026-08-20 fix
above already ruled out as the sole cause). 1024MB matches EVE-NG's real template
exactly - not a guess.
min_ram_mb ALSO raised to 1024 (not left at 512), found live while proving the fix
above: `providers/qemu.py`'s RAM-floor bump (`_eff_ram = int(node.ram or 512)`, then
bump only `if _eff_ram < _min_ram`) never fires when a caller creates a node with no
explicit `ram` at all, because `NodeDefinition.ram`'s own default (512) is NOT below
a min_ram_mb of 512 - the exact same "no unset-sentinel" gap this file's own qemu.py
comment already documents for `cpu` (bump only fires when the model default of 1 is
below the profile's cpu, which was always true for cpu but was never true for RAM
here since both defaulted to 512). Confirmed live: a node created with no explicit
ram genuinely booted at 512MB (`virsh dumpxml` showed `<memory unit='KiB'>524288`)
even with default_ram_mb=1024 above. EVE-NG's own viosl2.yml has only one RAM value
(1024) with no separate floor, so setting min == default here matches it exactly and
is the narrow, single-profile fix - NOT touching qemu.py's shared bump logic itself
(rule #26: that would change every other profile's floor behaviour too).
reasons.boot_timeout_sec:
boot_timeout_sec 400, not 240 (2026-08-22, LLA-074) - same IOSv-family boot-banner
evidence as "iosvl2"/"cisco-iosvl2" above, which already carry 400s for this exact
reason; this profile's node_config.py/serial_manager.py retry-window budgets scale
off this value, so 240s was cutting day-0 read windows short even before the
cpu_quota_period_us fix below existed.
reasons.virtio_extras:
virtio_extras=False (2026-08-20, Wave 3 real serial.log evidence, EVE-NG parity -
`-nodefaults`): IOSvL2 15.2.4.55e logs "%VIRTIO-3-INIT_FAIL ... PCI 0/6/0/1002" and
"PCI 0/7/0/1005 ... device is disabled, not supported" for libvirt's default
memballoon (0x1002) and rng (0x1005) devices on every boot. Omit both for this image.
reasons.cpu_quota_period_us:
cpu_quota_period_us=1000000 (LLA-074, 2026-08-22, unchanged): 1,000,000us is also
libvirt's hard ceiling for <cputune><global_period> ("Value of cputune 'global_period'
must be in range [1000, 1000000]", confirmed live 2026-09-29 trying to widen it further
for the NPX-1220 fix below - node start failed 422 on this exact schema error) - the
period cannot be widened past what LLA-074 already set.
reasons.cpu_quota_burst:
cpu_quota_burst=2.5 (2026-09-29, NPX-1220): period is already at libvirt's max (above),
so the only remaining lever against 1s-period throttling is the quota SIZE. Live cgroup
cpu.stat on a fresh viosl2-15.2.4.55e boot with this profile's real 12 e1000 NICs (EVE-NG
parity, not a test artifact), doing "crypto key generate rsa modulus 2048" at day-0,
reproduced identically across 3 separate node instances: nr_periods=122/nr_throttled=105
(86%) at the default 1x-cpu quota (providers/qemu.py's global_quota = cpu*period) - worse
than the 41% LLA-074 validated, because that validation never exercised this image's real
12-NIC topology. qemu.py's own <cputune> comment already documents this exact domain's
UNCAPPED usage peaking at 140-240% CPU (vcpu + emulator + per-NIC iothread work combined)
before global_quota was introduced to cap it at 100% - so a 2.5x quota multiplier still
caps well under that observed peak (never re-opening the original 140-240% runaway
`<cputune><quota>` was added to fix) while giving the emulator thread's 12-NIC I/O work
and the RSA keygen CPU spike enough combined headroom to land inside one 1s window
instead of tripping the hard cutoff mid-computation. `cpu` (vCPU count, still 1, EVE-NG
parity) is intentionally NOT raised - this widens only the burst ceiling the whole-domain
cgroup is allowed, not the guest's own visible core count. See providers/qemu.py's
`_cpu_quota_burst` for how this multiplies into <global_quota>.
